section: Quasi-judicial bodies - National Green Tribunal, NCLT/NCLAT, CAT, SAT, consumer commissions
subsections: Consumer commissions - pecuniary limits under Consumer Protection Act 2019
Tribunals Reforms Act 2021 - abolished tribunals, Madras Bar Association cases

accepted.s: Which one of the following was NOT created or introduced by the Consumer Protection Act, 2019?
o: Abolition of the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
accepted.x: The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 created the Central Consumer Protection Authority, three-tier Consumer Commissions and a product liability framework. It did not abolish the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission.
accepted.tq: Find the option that reverses a major institutional feature of the legislation.
accepted.sec: Consumer commissions - pecuniary limits under Consumer Protection Act 2019

accepted.s: The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 replaced which earlier legislation?
accepted.x: The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 replaced the Consumer Protection Act, 1986.
accepted.tq: Direct legislation-to-legislation recall.
accepted.sec: Consumer commissions - pecuniary limits under Consumer Protection Act 2019

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Consumer Protection Act, 2019:
1. It created the Central Consumer Protection Authority.
2. It provides for a three-tier structure of District, State and National Consumer Commissions.
3. It introduced product liability.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The 2019 Act created the Central Consumer Protection Authority, retained a three-tier commission structure and introduced product liability.
accepted.tq: Check each institutional feature before selecting the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Consumer commissions - pecuniary limits under Consumer Protection Act 2019

accepted.s: Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, which of the following procedural facilities was introduced?
o: Hearing of complaints only through physical appearance
Mandatory trial only before the Supreme Court
Automatic transfer of all complaints to High Courts
E-filing of complaints and hearings through videoconference
accepted.x: The Act introduced e-filing of complaints and hearings through videoconference.
accepted.tq: Identify the option reflecting the digital-procedure reform.
accepted.sec: Consumer commissions - pecuniary limits under Consumer Protection Act 2019

accepted.s: A complaint is not decided within 21 days of filing. Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, what is the consequence mentioned in the legislation?
o: It is deemed to have been dismissed
It is automatically transferred to the National Commission
It is deemed to have been admitted
accepted.x: A complaint not decided within 21 days is deemed to have been admitted.
accepted.tq: Use the precise statutory time limit and distinguish admission from dismissal.
accepted.sec: Consumer commissions - pecuniary limits under Consumer Protection Act 2019

accepted.s: Under the 2021 Rules, a consumer complaint involving consideration of ₹40 lakh falls within the original pecuniary jurisdiction of which body?
accepted.x: Under the 2021 Rules, the District Commission has jurisdiction over matters up to ₹50 lakh.
accepted.tq: Apply the lower pecuniary threshold to a concrete fact situation.
accepted.sec: Consumer commissions - pecuniary limits under Consumer Protection Act 2019

accepted.s: Under the pecuniary limits prescribed by the 2021 Rules, which range is correctly matched with the State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission?
accepted.x: The State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has pecuniary jurisdiction from ₹50 lakh to ₹2 crore under the 2021 Rules.
accepted.tq: Compare adjacent jurisdictional bands and avoid using the older statutory limits.
accepted.sec: Consumer commissions - pecuniary limits under Consumer Protection Act 2019

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the pecuniary jurisdiction of the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission under the 2021 Rules?
accepted.x: Under the 2021 Rules, the National Commission has jurisdiction over complaints involving consideration above ₹2 crore.
accepted.tq: Test the revised threshold against the older ₹1 crore and ₹10 crore figures.
accepted.sec: Consumer commissions - pecuniary limits under Consumer Protection Act 2019

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. District Consumer Commission — Up to ₹50 lakh
2. State Consumer Commission — ₹50 lakh to ₹2 crore
3. National Consumer Commission — Above ₹2 crore
accepted.x: All three pairs correctly state the pecuniary jurisdiction under the 2021 Rules.
accepted.tq: Verify the continuity and boundaries of the three jurisdictional slabs.
accepted.sec: Consumer commissions - pecuniary limits under Consumer Protection Act 2019

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission:
1. It was set up in 1988.
2. Its President may be a sitting or retired Judge of the Supreme Court or a Chief Justice of a High Court.
3. An original order of the Commission may be appealed to the Supreme Court within 30 days.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The NCDRC was set up in 1988; its President is drawn from the specified senior judicial positions, and an original order can be appealed to the Supreme Court within 30 days.
accepted.tq: Combine establishment, qualification and appeal-period facts in one institutional check.
accepted.sec: Consumer commissions - pecuniary limits under Consumer Protection Act 2019

accepted.s: The 2021 Madras Bar Association case dealt with provisions of which instrument that were struck down for defying earlier rulings?
accepted.x: In the 2021 Madras Bar Association case, provisions of the Tribunals Reforms Ordinance were struck down because they defied earlier judicial rulings.
accepted.tq: Match the case year with the specific legislative instrument involved.
accepted.sec: Tribunals Reforms Act 2021 - abolished tribunals, Madras Bar Association cases

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the 2025 Madras Bar Association case?
o: It struck down the re-enacted provisions and restored the earlier framework.
It transferred all tribunal functions to the Supreme Court.
It upheld all provisions re-enacted by Parliament without modification.
It abolished the National Tribunals Commission.
accepted.x: The 2025 Madras Bar Association case struck down provisions re-enacted by Parliament and restored the earlier framework.
accepted.tq: Watch for the reversal trap between upholding and striking down re-enacted provisions.
accepted.sec: Tribunals Reforms Act 2021 - abolished tribunals, Madras Bar Association cases

accepted.s: The National Tribunals Commission was first recommended in which case?
accepted.x: The National Tribunals Commission was first recommended in the Rojer Mathew case of 2019.
accepted.tq: Link the recommendation to the correct case and year instead of the later implementation discussion.
accepted.sec: Tribunals Reforms Act 2021 - abolished tribunals, Madras Bar Association cases

accepted.s: The Supreme Court gave the government how much time in the 2025 Madras Bar Association case to set up a National Tribunals Commission?
accepted.x: The Supreme Court gave the government four months to establish a National Tribunals Commission.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact compliance period attached to the judicial direction.
accepted.sec: Tribunals Reforms Act 2021 - abolished tribunals, Madras Bar Association cases

accepted.s: What principle was laid down in R. Gandhi (2010) regarding tribunal members performing judicial functions?
o: They must be nominated by consumer commissions.
They must be appointed exclusively by the executive.
They must be independent of the executive.
accepted.x: R. Gandhi (2010) held that tribunal members performing judicial functions must remain independent of the executive.
accepted.tq: Identify the constitutional principle from the case rather than the appointing authority.
accepted.sec: Tribunals Reforms Act 2021 - abolished tribunals, Madras Bar Association cases

accepted.s: In the Essel Infraprojects insolvency case, the Supreme Court set aside orders of which bodies because they relied on AI-generated fictitious citations?
accepted.x: The Supreme Court set aside the NCLT and NCLAT orders in the Essel Infraprojects insolvency case because they relied on AI-generated fictitious citations.
accepted.tq: Use the wrong-body trap to distinguish the insolvency tribunals from other quasi-judicial bodies.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s:
Which of the following recent developments is correctly matched with the concerned body?
1. Suo motu cognisance of delays — NCLT
2. Report on 5.7 lakh pending consumer cases — NCDRC
3. Orders set aside for AI-generated fictitious citations — NCLT and NCLAT
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correctly matched. The Supreme Court took suo motu cognisance of NCLT delays, sought an NCDRC report on 5.7 lakh pending cases, and set aside the NCLT-NCLAT orders in the Essel matter.
accepted.tq: Start with the distinctive numerical figure and then verify the remaining body-event pairs.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The Supreme Court took suo motu cognisance of delays in which tribunal?
accepted.x: The Supreme Court took suo motu cognisance of delays in the National Company Law Tribunal.
accepted.tq: Direct body-to-development identification.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding staffing and infrastructure concerns associated with tribunals?
o: Over 95% of NCLT administrative staff are contractual, and NGT lacks an IT division.
NGT has an IT division but no parent ministry funding.
Over 95% of NGT administrative staff are contractual, and NCLT lacks an IT division.
TDSAT has had 95% permanent staff since 2001.
accepted.x: Over 95% of NCLT's administrative staff are contractual, while the NGT lacks an IT division.
accepted.tq: Separate the tribunal, percentage and deficiency instead of accepting swapped institutional details.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Since 2001, the staff strength of the Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal has been fixed at:
accepted.x: TDSAT's staff strength has remained fixed at 52 posts since 2001.
accepted.tq: Recall the precise staffing figure and reject nearby rounded values.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Tribunals are generally funded by their parent ministries. In the case of the National Green Tribunal, the parent ministry is:
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
accepted.x: The National Green Tribunal is funded by its parent ministry, the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
accepted.tq: Ask which ministry would logically correspond to the tribunal's subject jurisdiction.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding tribunals in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: NCLT has an Amravati bench, and the AP Cooperative Tribunal functions under Section 75 of the AP Cooperative Societies Act, 1964.
NCLT has a Vijayawada bench, and the AP Cooperative Tribunal functions under Section 52 of the Act.
NCLT has an Amravati bench, and the AP Cooperative Tribunal functions under Section 75 of the Companies Act, 2013.
NCLT has no bench in Andhra Pradesh, and the AP Cooperative Tribunal is established under the Tribunals Reforms Act, 2021.
accepted.x: The NCLT has an Amravati bench. The AP Cooperative Tribunal is constituted under Section 75 of the Andhra Pradesh Cooperative Societies Act, 1964.
accepted.tq: Check both the local location and the exact statutory basis.
accepted.sec: Universal angles
